summary: Every row has 2 more seats than the row in front, so the rows hold S, S+2, S+4, … seats — an arithmetic sequence. We simply walk through the R rows and add them up (T1 — direct formula / simple loop).

blocks.title: Read S first, then R
blocks.text: The two numbers come on two separate lines, so we need two `input()` calls. Order matters: the judge types S first, so reading R first would swap the values. `int()` turns the typed text into a number we can do math with.

blocks.title: Set up the running total
blocks.text: `total` starts at 0 and `seats` holds the size of the row we are looking at, starting with the first row S. The comment reminds us the pattern is S, S+2, S+4, …

blocks.title: Add one row at a time
blocks.text: `range(R)` runs exactly R times — one pass per row. We add the current row first, then grow `seats` by 2 for the next row. If you swapped these two lines, the first row would be counted as S+2. `range(R + 1)` would add one row too many.

blocks.title: Formula check and output
blocks.text: The comment gives the closed form `S*R + R*(R-1)`, great for checking a sample by hand (10, 4 → 40 + 12 = 52). The f-string prints exactly `Total seats: 52` — keep the space after the colon, the judge compares character by character.

complexity: Time O(R) with R ≤ 1000 → at most 1,000 additions, instant.
pitfalls: Reading R before S — the prompts ask for S first.
